title: Left-right partners had smaller downstream response distances than matched pairs in two partial adult worm electrical models
abstract: We tested whether left-right neuron partners give less distinct remote responses than matched other pairs in passive electrical models of two partial adult worm maps. At uniform leak 0.1 relative to mean weighted degree, median response-distance ratios were 0.705 for 62 partner pairs in map 7 and 0.673 for 67 in map 8. Controls matched source strength, direct-link presence and approximate mutual count. Removing the mutual link separately for each tested and control pair left ratios of 0.728 and 0.668. Tighter matching and disjoint-source controls also gave ratios below one. A rank-one inverse identity gives exact mutual-link attenuation and passed independent numerical checks. The contrast became smaller at larger leak. The results apply to count-weighted passive models with equal current inputs and fixed observation noise. Partial annotations, assumed conductances, missing chemical and active signaling, and unmeasured noise prevent a claim about biological decoding or transfer across species. Code, graph arrays, provenance, controls and a figure permit reproduction.

display.caption: Remote source-distance ratios under matched controls and direct-link removal in two partial adult worm models. Lower ratios mean less separated partner responses under fixed equal observation noise. Leak is an assumed model parameter.

citations.reason: Uses the same raw maps and passive model; this work tests source separation, matched controls and mutual-link removal. No numerical outputs or code reused.
